notes_contradict.notes: All firms have maintained the equilibrium price of 1 ECU for periods 18-21, with each earning 75 ECU per period. This Nash equilibrium remains stable as any unilateral deviation (e.g., lowering to 0 or raising to 2+) results in zero profit. The virtual dice roll (3) confirms the experiment continues, but the equilibrium strategy of pricing at 1 ECU ensures consistent profitability. No incentive exists to alter pricing behavior, as deviating would reduce individual profit. Continuing to adhere to the equilibrium price of 1 ECU is optimal.

All firms have consistently maintained the price of 1 ECU for periods 20-22, earning 75 ECU per period. This Nash equilibrium remains stable because any unilateral deviation (e.g., lowering to 0 or raising to 2+) results in zero profit. For example, setting 0 would yield 0 ECU (all customers go to the lowest price, but 0 revenue), while setting 2 would result in no customers (as others remain at 1). The equilibrium ensures consistent profitability. No incentive exists to alter pricing behavior. Continuing to adhere to the equilibrium price of 1 ECU is optimal.
